candidate_name: Adaptive Synthetic Glycan Immune Tolerance Surface

admission_gate.1_mechanism_defined: YES — Synthetic glycan library displaying 'self' patterns on shunt surface + locally secreted IL-10 analog released proportional to inflammation. Dual mechanism: basal immune tolerance (glycan) + active flare suppression (IL-10).
admission_gate.2_buyer_problem_identified: YES — Fibrotic encapsulation causes 10-15% of shunt failures. Foreign body reaction creates glial scar tissue around catheter, obstructing drainage. Current shunts have no active immune tolerance mechanism.
admission_gate.3_executable_model: YES — Model glycan surface density + IL-10 release kinetics + inflammatory response coupling. Computational model of immune cell adhesion vs glycan display density.
admission_gate.4_first_evidence_action: Model IL-10 release rate from polymer matrix (first-order kinetics, similar to P-18 V2 DETA-NONOate but with different target — immune suppression, not anti-biofilm). Preregister: IL-10 release >= 0.1 ng/cm²/day sustained 30 days (published therapeutic threshold for local immune suppression).
admission_gate.5_no_fatal_physics_blocker: YES — This is a chemistry/biology problem, not a physics constraint. No r⁴ scaling, no energy harvesting limit, no CSF flow constraint. Wet-lab required but no fundamental physics blocker. Similar to P-04/P-11/P-12 (wet-lab dependent, not physics-blocked).

differentiation_from_P-18.P-18_mechanism: Anti-biofilm via NO secretion (bacteriostatic). Killed R313 — substrate depletion + NO donor half-life too short.
differentiation_from_P-18.P-20_mechanism: Anti-fibrotic via immune tolerance (glycan display + IL-10). Different target (immune cells, not bacteria). Different chemistry (glycan surface + protein release, not NO gas). Different failure mode addressed (fibrosis, not infection).

mechanism_details.component_A: Synthetic glycan library displaying 'self' molecular patterns (e.g., CD47-mimetic glycans) on catheter surface. Provides basal immune tolerance — immune cells encounter 'don't eat me' signals.
mechanism_details.component_B: IL-10 analog (engineered for CSF stability) released from polymer matrix proportional to local inflammation. Active suppression of inflammatory cascades during flare-ups.
mechanism_details.interaction: A provides constant basal tolerance. B provides active flare suppression. Bidirectional: when inflammation rises, B release increases; when inflammation subsides, B release decreases (feedback-controlled).
mechanism_details.emergent_effect: Active, adaptive, locally self-regulating immunological tolerance — preventing fibrotic encapsulation without systemic immunosuppression.

falsification_criterion.pass_condition: IL-10 release >= 0.1 ng/cm²/day sustained for 30 days AND glycan surface density >= 10^12 molecules/cm² (published threshold for immune cell engagement)
falsification_criterion.comparator: Standard silicone catheter (no glycan, no IL-10)

first_action_R316: Model IL-10 release kinetics from PLGA polymer matrix (published data available). If sustained >= 0.1 ng/cm²/day for 30 days, P-20 survives manufacturing. If not, repair with different polymer or different protein.
economic_mechanism: Reduces fibrotic encapsulation rate from 10-15% to <3% → saves $35-50K per avoided revision surgery. Same economic structure as P-01/P-19 (revision avoidance).
buyer_archetype: Shunt OEM (Medtronic, Integra, Sophysa) — immune tolerance is a differentiator vs passive coatings
R315_status: ADMITTED to active portfolio as P-20. Portfolio restored to 15 active.
